textbookText: discovered by Dutch naturalist Anton Van Leeuwenhoek in 1675. The branch of biology that deals with the study of bacteria is called bacteriology.

Bacteria are the smallest of all known cellular organisms. The average size of bacterial cells ranges from 0.5μm to 1.5 μm in diameter. The shape of bacteria and forms of individual bacteria are usually constant while some can change their shape and size with changes in environmental conditions. This ability of organisms is known as pleiomorphism. For example; Corenebacteria, Legionella pneumophila etc.
On the basis of shape, bacteria are classified into following groups: 1. Cocci (Sing. Coccus) 2. Bacilli (Sing. Bacillus) 3. Helical bacteria 4. Filamentous bacteria
1. Cocci (Sing. Coccus)
These are spherical, oval or rounded in shape. They are non-motile as they lack flagella. They are found in different forms:
Monococcus (Occurs Singly)
Diplococcus (Occurs in pairs)
Te tracoccus (occurs in tetrad)
Stre ptococcus (Occurs in chain)
Staphylococcus (Occurs in cluster)
Sarcina (occurs cubical packet)

STRUCTURE OF BACTERIAL CELL They usually have a simple structure without organized nucleus and membrane- bounded cell organelles such as mitochondria, golgi bodies, plastids, etc. A typical bacterial cell is Biology, Grade 11 | 171

surrounded by a rigid, protective covering called cell wall which is made up of peptidoglycan, mucopeptide or murein. The cell wall gives proper shape and protects the cell against mechanical injury, chemicals and pathogens. Inner to cell wall, bacterial cell contains a thin, elastic, semi-permeable membrane called plasma membrane. The inner surface of the plasma membrane consists of several respiratory enzymes which help in respiration. In some bacteria , the plasma membrane gives rise to infoldings called mesosomes that play an important role during respiration and cell division. Externally, the cell wall is covered with a gelatinous substance called slime layer. In some bacteria, these slime layer forms a thick covering due to addition of amino acids, called capsule. The bacteria having capsule is called as capsulated bacteria. Capsule or slime layer protect the cells from chemicals and desiccation. In some bacteria, hairs like structure called pili are present on the cell wall that helps in attachment with host.

Figure 3.1.6 Structure of a typical bacterial cell Inside the cell membrane granular, colourless fluids are present called protoplasm. It consists of 70s ribosome, gas vacuoles (present in aquatic form for floatation), reserve food materials (like, glycogen, lipid, protein etc.), centrally located circular double-stranded, naked DNA (incipient nucleus). Along with the normal DNA chromosomes, many bacteria also have extrachromosomal genetic elements or DNA called plasmid. Photosynthetic bacteria consist of thylakoids called chromatophore which consists of photosynthetic pigments. The motile bacteria consists of fine, thread-like, protoplasmic attachments called as flagella. Flagella are absent in capsulated bacteria.
